comparator.name: Theology
comparator.sourceNotes: Tilburg University's official 2026-2027 curriculum, checked 2026-09-29, describes one 180-ECTS Theology bachelor delivered in English at Tilburg and in Dutch at Utrecht, with full-time three-year and mostly content-equivalent part-time pacing. The English full-time Tilburg route is used because it is the target-named English route and supplies the current 60+60+60 academic sequence. To avoid inventing a missing course title, the first four semester curricula are preserved as 30-ECTS blocks. The published year-one course rows total 30 ECTS in each semester. The year-two first-semester rows display 27 ECTS although the 180-ECTS programme, two 60-ECTS surrounding years and the page's explicit research-methods/academic-skills statement require a 60-ECTS second year; the semester block therefore preserves the official 30-ECTS allocation while transparently noting the three-credit display gap. Year three consists of a 30-ECTS mobility/minor window and a 30-ECTS courses-and-thesis block. The resulting six components total exactly 180 ECTS.
components: Year 1, semester 1: foundations in theology, scripture, religion, philosophy and Christian history
Biblical Hebrew 1 (3), Theological Seminar (3), Bible and Exegesis: Introduction (6), Comparative Religion (6), History of Philosophy (6), and History of European Christianity (6).
Year 1, semester 2: languages, dogmatics, ethics, spirituality, philosophy and practical theology

Biblical Hebrew 2 (3), Greek 1 (3), Fundamental Theology and Dogmatics (6), Ethics and Character (3), Spirituality: Introduction (3), Systematic Philosophy (6), and Practical Theology: Introduction (6).
Year 2, semester 1: advanced theology, religious studies, languages, law and scripture

The official table lists Greek 2 (3), Latin 1 (3), Dogmatics: Christ and Trinity (6), Sociology and Psychology of Religion (6), Canon Law: Introduction (3), Judaism: Introduction (3), and Old Testament: Torah and Prophetic Literature (3), totaling 27 ECTS. The page separately states that year two deepens disciplinary research methods and academic skills; the 30-ECTS semester block is retained without fabricating the omitted three-credit course title.
Year 2, semester 2: language, biblical interpretation, church history, dogmatics and Jewish studies

Latin 2 (3), New Testament: Synoptic Gospels and Johannine Literature (6), Church History: Middle Ages and Modernity (6), Dogmatics: Creation, Church and Completion (6), Judaism: Reading Rabbinic Texts (3), New Testament: Acts and Letters (3), and Old Testament: Wisdom Literature and Psalms (3). Several listed courses rotate annually between years 2 and 3.
Choose one official 30-ECTS option: exchange/study abroad, Theology electives, Theology and Philosophy courses for the canonical degree, or another Tilburg University minor.
Year 3 courses and Bachelor Thesis in Theology

Bachelor Thesis in Theology (9), Catholic Ethics in Practice (6), Liturgy and Sacraments (6), Philosophy of Religion and Metaphysics (3), Moral Philosophy (3), and Patristics (3); several courses rotate annually between years 2 and 3.

routeSelection.basis: The registry target is displayed in English as Theology and includes the English Tilburg and Dutch Utrecht deliveries. The official English programme page expressly identifies Tilburg as the English location, and the three-year full-time route provides the neutral 180-ECTS academic structure aligned with the fixed three-year UCR comparison cohort. Part-time delivery is mostly the same content at a slower pace, not a distinct academic specialization.

exception.reason: The programme's defining academic identity is Catholic theology and theology-specific method: biblical Hebrew, Greek and Latin; Old and New Testament exegesis; fundamental and systematic theology; dogmatics; spirituality; practical theology; liturgy and sacraments; church history; canon law; Judaism; Catholic ethics; patristics; and an independent Theology thesis. Only the 30-ECTS mobility/minor window is broadly open. UCR offers adjacent philosophy, ethics, history, sociology, politics, law, literature and cultural analysis, but no sustained theology, scripture, source-language, liturgical or pastoral curriculum. Constructing a 24-course UCR programme from those neighbouring fields would remove the target's defining theological sequence and misrepresent it as a substantive match.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official 2026-2027 page establishes a 180-ECTS bachelor with complete 60-ECTS first- and third-year structures and a second year devoted to deeper theological disciplines, source languages, religious studies and research skills. The displayed year-two first-semester course rows total 27 ECTS, leaving a transparent three-credit display gap. The comparator therefore preserves each semester as a 30-ECTS block rather than inventing a missing course identity. The English full-time Tilburg route is academically representative; the Dutch Utrecht and part-time deliveries are language/pacing variants, while the optional canonical-degree package remains one choice inside the 30-ECTS mobility window.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook course rows, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. GOSPHIL111, GOSPHIL212, GOSPHIL214, GOSPHIL311 and GOSPHIL313 support philosophy, ethics, mind, emotion, agency and the self; GOSHIST111, GOSHIST211 and GOSHIST312 support historical inquiry; GOSSOCI111, GOSSOCI214 and GOSSOCI311 support social analysis; MCCLITR112 and MCCLITR211 encounter literary and mythic traditions; GOSLAWJ111 and GOSLAWJ213 touch law, rights and constitutional treatment of religion-adjacent issues. None is a dedicated course in Catholic or systematic theology, biblical Hebrew/Greek/Latin, scriptural exegesis, dogmatics, spirituality, practical theology, liturgy, sacraments, canon law, patristics or theological research. Isolated adjacent humanities and social-science courses cannot support a defensible 24-course Theology progression.
